name: Ossian Perforated Moto Jacket
description:
A fitted motorcycle jacket in full-grain cowhide, black with a slight pull-up finish that shows the leather's natural character under light. The cut is asymmetric-zip, with a wide lapel that can be snapped closed at the throat, perforated panels across the shoulders and upper sleeves for airflow, and four exterior pockets — two slash at the hip, one zip at the chest, one welt at the collar. The lining is a slick viscose in deep burgundy. No padding, no armor, no tech. Just a very good leather jacket.

Ossian is a Tier 3 independent, one of a handful of labels still doing genuine leather goods in GLMZ. They source from synthetic-free ranches in the Wisconsin interior and tan in small batches. The perforated moto has been in their line for fifteen years with minimal changes because nothing about it needs changing. It's the kind of jacket that looks better at forty hours than it does at zero.
what_it_says: You have personal style that didn't come from an algorithm. You understand quality and you're willing to pay for it without needing to tell anyone.
story_hooks: Ossian's leather supplier has gone dark — three weeks without contact, and the last shipment arrived with a hide that had been branded with a mark no one at Ossian recognizes.
A specific Ossian moto jacket keeps appearing in security footage across three districts over six months — always in the background, always in motion, never showing the wearer's face.

A Tier 5 collector is paying absurd premiums for first-run Ossian pieces, claiming they contain trace compounds from an extinct tanning process — the current owners of those jackets have no idea why they're suddenly targets.
